content.overview: Inspection can spread contamination or erase scope if people, tools and samples move without control. The workflow should protect workers, unaffected material and evidence identity.

vocabulary.definition: Controls that limit movement or processing while evidence is evaluated.
Planned order of observations that reduces cross-transfer and preserves context.
Maintained identity and condition of a sample from collection through analysis.

sections.title: Plan clean-to-suspect movement
sections.body: Defined routes, tools, PPE and sanitation reduce transfer between unaffected and suspect material.

sections.title: Map units before disturbing them
sections.body: Location, container, rack and lot identity should be captured before sampling or movement changes the pattern.

sections.title: Samples remain linked to source
sections.body: Unique IDs, collection details and transfer records preserve what each result can support.

workedExamples: A suspect rack is mapped and contained before individual samples are collected with separate tools and source IDs.
commonMistakes: Inspecting suspect then unaffected material with the same tool.
Moving units to make inspection easier without updating genealogy.
content.practicalApplication: Write a clean-to-suspect inspection route with tool control, mapping, sample IDs, PPE and stop/escalation points.
content.summary: Sanitary inspection preserves both material control and the spatial evidence needed for defensible scope.
